title: Prefetch consensus protocol for cross-device kernel selection and NCCL overlap steering
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The current multi-GPU prefill/decode path suffers from transient tail latency due to mismatched kernel hints and suboptimal NCCL scheduling windows. Devices independently choose kernel variants (FP16/INT8 kernels, attention tiling strategies) based on local heuristics which sometimes diverge for the same request wave. That divergence forces extra synchronization or produces non-overlapped NCCL patterns, increasing p95/p99 latency for prefill and early decode tokens.

Goal:
Design and implement a lightweight consensus protocol that runs during the prefill handshake to achieve two outcomes: (1) agree on kernel-selection hints and attention tiling parameters for the upcoming request wave, and (2) coordinate NCCL communication ordering to maximize overlap between computation and comm. The protocol should be low-latency (<= 250us extra per prefill), robust to stragglers, and incrementally deployable behind a feature flag.

Approach/Design:
1) Prefetch consensus message (PCM): each device emits a compact vote containing: model variant id, preferred kernel id, sequence-length bucket, and estimated KV cache size. Votes are piggybacked on existing rendezvous control messages or sent via a short TCP control channel when NCCL bootstrap isn't sufficient.
2) Stage leader election: elect a per-wave leader deterministically (e.g., lowest GPU rank in the rendezvous group or hash of request id) to compute the merged kernel plan. The leader returns an authoritative plan to all participants.
3) Merge rules and hedging: leader applies deterministic merge: choose kernel variant that maximizes a scored utility function (latency estimate, memory fit, quantization compatibility). If incompatible votes exist (heterogeneous devices), leader suggests a fallback plan with asymmetric kernels + a timed NCCL window to preserve overlap.
4) NCCL overlap steering: along with kernel hints, the leader emits a comm-ordering sequence and reservation windows (start/length in microseconds) that devices use to arrange prefetches and chunk sizes. The intent is to stagger comm bursts to reduce contention and increase compute overlap.
5) Fallbacks and safety: if consensus timeout exceeds threshold (default 1ms), devices fall back to current local heuristic. Protocol supports version negotiation to remain compatible with older nodes.

Implementation notes:
- Integrate PCM into the existing rendezvous layer (rendezvous control path lives in cpp/runtime/rendezvous). Add a PCM serializer with a 32B compact footprint.
- Leader codepath will live under cpp/runtime/scheduler/consensus_leader.{h,cc}. Keep the leader work minimal — no blocking I/O on the hot path.
- Telemetry: emit per-wave tags: consensus_latency_us, chosen_kernel_id, percentage_votes_mapped, comm_window_utilization. Surface these in Console per-route dashboards.
- Feature flag: runtime.consensus_prefetch = off by default. Controlled rollout via console rollout policies (canary 5% then 25% then 100%).

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Rollout gating: no increase in error rate or observed p99 tail > 10% compared to baseline during canary.
- Quantitative targets (on Dedicated clusters under mixed load): reduce p99 prefill latency by >= 12% and increase NCCL overlap utilization by >= 18% on average for long-sequence (>=2048 token) requests.
- CPU overhead: additional host CPU due to consensus <= 5% on conductor/worker processes.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Centralized scheduler: rejected because it requires additional control-plane scaling and adds single-point-of-failure and cross-customer isolation concerns.
- Fully peer-to-peer: we considered a fully decentralized policy where devices converge via multiple round-trips, but that increased control latency beyond acceptable bounds.
- Machine-learning predictor for kernel selection: promising but outside scope for MVP; would be a follow-up (see sub_issues).

Rollout and test plan:
- Unit tests for PCM serialization/forwarding, leader election determinism, and timeout behavior.
- Integration tests in CI with simulated heterogeneous GPU pool (A100 + H100) to validate merge rules and fallbacks.
- Perf job: a synthetic replay harness (perf/replays/long_seq_2k) with 48h baseline and 48h post-change comparing p50/p95/p99 and NCCL overlap traces.
- Canary: enable on a small Dedicated cluster (canary label) for 72h, monitor the Console dashboard (link in comments).

Follow-ups (post-MVP):
- Add ML-based kernel-prediction component that uses historical wave telemetry.
- Expose per-tenant knobs for aggressiveness of NCCL steering.
- Extend protocol to support on-prem air-gapped deployments over secured control channel.
